help.title: What is automation for?
help.body:
## What is an automation?

An **automation** starts a loop on its own, using a blueprint you chose, so you do not have to start it by hand. There are three kinds:

- **Schedule**: starts on a cron time, in a timezone, optionally only inside a time window.
- **Webhook**: starts when something calls the daemon with the right secret. Only the *name* of the secret variable is stored here, never its value.
- **Event**: starts when something happens inside Aeon, such as a task finishing, that matches the filter you set.

## Safe by default

- A new automation is created **disarmed**. Enabling it is a separate, deliberate act, and the daemon states exactly what you are authorising.
- You can **archive** an automation, but never delete it. Unarchiving brings it back disarmed.
- Every start attempt is recorded in the **fire log** with one of five outcomes: started, refused, limited, skipped, or could-not-say.
- An agent may only *propose* narrowing an automation. Nothing is applied until you commit it under **Proposals**.

hint.automations: Open one to see what it does, its health and its history, or to enable, pause, fire or archive it.

webhook.presetGithubIssue: GitHub: a new issue is opened
webhook.presetGithubPr: GitHub: a pull request is opened
webhook.customHint: Name the event as the sender calls it (the X-GitHub-Event header for GitHub), then optionally its actions after a colon, for example issues:opened,reopened. Any other signed delivery is answered and ignored.
webhook.ignoredHint: Any other signed delivery (a ping, a push, an issue being edited) is answered and ignored, so it never starts a loop.
webhook.goalHint: Fields of the delivery go in curly brackets and are filled in when it arrives. They go in as short single-line text; the whole delivery still reaches the loop as untrusted data. For example:
webhook.connectSteps: In the repository: Settings, Webhooks, Add webhook. Use the payload URL above with the address of your daemon, content type application/json, and the same secret that is in the variable named above; under events pick the one you chose here. The daemon must be started with --http and be reachable from GitHub.
